en: The Question on the Simile of the Buddha.
"Yes, Great King, the Blessed One exists."
“But is it possible, venerable Nāgasena, to point out the Buddha here or there?
“The Blessed One, Great King, has attained final Nibbāna in the element of Nibbāna without residue; it is not possible to point out the Blessed One as being ‘here’ or ‘there.
“What do you think, great king? When the flame of a great mass of blazing fire has gone out, is it possible to point to that flame and say, ‘It is here’ or ‘It is there’?
“No, venerable sir, that flame has ceased; it has passed into non-designation.
“In the same way, great king, the Blessed One has attained final Nibbāna in the element of Nibbāna without residue; he has gone out.”
"It is not possible, O Blessed One, to point him out as being 'here' or 'there'; rather, Great King, it is by means of the body of Dhamma that the Blessed One can be pointed out.
For the Dhamma, Great King, was taught by the Blessed One."
Thus ends the tenth question, on the illustration of the Buddha.
This is the fifth chapter, the Chapter on the Buddha.
In this chapter, there are ten questions.
